counts_closing_quote: All in violation of Title 18, United States Code, Section 1343.

forfeiture.notes: If convicted of any of Counts 1-4, forfeiture of proceeds-traceable property; substitute-asset allegation under § 853(p). No dollar amount is stated in the forfeiture paragraphs.

amounts.quote: In all, between approximately March 2023 and August 2025, SALLAH and his company fraudulently claimed to be entitled to approximately $1.4 million for providing Housing Stabilization Services and received nearly $1.3 million.
amounts.notes: Same paragraph as the $1.3 million received figure; do not add $1.4M + $1.3M. Restated as claimed-entitled about $1.4 million in para 23. CHARGED_ALLEGED, not proven_loss. Do not add to first-wave HSS or FOF.

amounts.quote: In all, between approximately March 2023 and August 2025, SALLAH and his company fraudulently claimed to be entitled to approximately $1.4 million for providing Housing Stabilization Services and received nearly $1.3 million.
amounts.notes: Face language is received nearly $1.3 million — amount_paid to the provider, not proven_loss. Same paragraph as $1.4M claimed; do not add. Schema has no amount_received; amount_paid is the matching metric. Do not add to first-wave HSS or FOF.

amounts.quote: Ultimately, SALLAH fraudulently claimed to service nearly 150 different beneficiaries through SafeLodgings and for such services claimed to be entitled to about $1.4 million.
amounts.notes: Same ~$1.4M claimed-entitled as para 13; do not sum. Also alleges nearly 150 purported beneficiaries and that operations provided only a fraction of the claimed total.

amounts.quote: SALLAH diverted much of his fraud proceeds to conspirators, including to his employees at SafeLodgings, and he spent much of it on himself and on investments, including nearly $150,000 in a cryptocurrency exchange.
amounts.notes: Alleged diversion of proceeds into a cryptocurrency exchange — not a Medicaid billed or paid figure and not an additional loss on top of the $1.3M received. Overlaps the received $1.3M. Do not add to first-wave HSS or FOF.

program_rate_recitals_not_case_totals.quote: Consultants could bill Medicaid about $174 for a consulting session.
program_rate_recitals_not_case_totals.notes: Statewide HSS rate recital, not a SafeLodgings total.

program_rate_recitals_not_case_totals.quote: Providers can bill about $68 per hour of transition services provided.
Moving expenses of up to $3,000, subject to conditions.
Before the Program’s inaugural year, DHS predicted the Program would cost about $2.6 million annually.
program_rate_recitals_not_case_totals.notes: DHS prediction recital, not this case.

statewide_hss_program_payouts_recital.quote: In 2021 alone, the Program paid out more than $21 million in claims. That figure ballooned in the following years: $42 million in 2022, $74 million in 2023, $104 million in 2024. In just the first six months of 2025, the Program paid out another $61 million.
statewide_hss_program_payouts_recital.notes: Statewide HSS program_spend recitals, not Sallah alleged_loss. Identical boilerplate also appears in Aden/Falade/Hussein. Already claimed; do not invent a second program-spend claim. Do not add these to SafeLodgings $1.4M/$1.3M, first-wave HSS, or FOF $250M.

leo_human_services_mention.quote: One of SALLAH’s employees, Employee A, had previously worked at another HSS Provider, Leo Human Services. Employee A had been fired from Leo—which itself submitted millions of dollars in fraudulent HSS bills—because Employee A’s fraudulent conduct at that company was too brazen.
leo_human_services_mention.notes: Recital about Employee A’s prior employment at Leo Human Services. Not a charging document against Asad Adow / Leo. The 'millions of dollars' phrase is qualitative and is not a new Leo dollar claim; Asad/Leo remains the first-wave $2.7M amount_paid allegation. Do not add Sallah dollars to Asad.

other_face_facts: Para 1: scheme to fraudulently receive Medicaid benefits from Minnesota's Housing Stability Services Program; alleged misappropriation of more than a million dollars (qualitative; overlaps the $1.4M/$1.3M figures, do not treat as a third case total).
Face stamp: SCANNED DEC 16 2025 U.S. DISTRICT COURT MPLS.
Para 10-11: Sallah owned and operated SafeLodgings, Inc.; registered with MN SOS in March 2023 and enrolled as HSS provider the same month.
Para 17: purported to service individuals from a building in Forest Lake, Minnesota.
Para 18: Sallah responsible for billing; bills submitted through a third-party EHR company on a subscription; alleged inflated and fraudulent bills.
Para 19: alleged double billing — employees claimed to service multiple beneficiaries in the same one- or two-hour blocks.
Para 20: Sallah claimed to have personally provided more than 3,600 billable service hours in 2024 alone, including double billing. Hours, not a dollar figure.

Para 24: November 2025 grand jury subpoena for company records; Sallah retained counsel then fled; on or about November 26 flew MSP to Amsterdam and has not returned. Flight is a face allegation, not a count.
Page 8 is signature page (A TRUE BILL / UNITED STATES ATTORNEY / FOREPERSON); no additional counts.
related_to_asad_adow: Named in 0:25-cr-00354 ECF 18 reassignment of related case 25-CR-482 (SRN/DLM) to Judge Blackwell. Not a charging instrument against Asad Adow.
do_not: Do not add $1.4M claimed + $1.3M received + $150k crypto + statewide program payouts + qualitative 'more than a million'.
Do not add SafeLodgings dollars to first-wave HSS (Aden/Falade/Anwar/Asad) or to FOF $250M.
Do not treat the Leo Human Services recital as a charge against Asad Adow.
Do not treat $ figures in this indictment as proven_loss.
Do not invent a second statewide HSS program_spend claim; overlap_group already claimed.
